Pankaj Kumar Kundu, Advocate ------ For the Petitioner. 
Jahangir Alam, Advocate ------ For the Respondent No.2.
parties:
Ziaur Rahman (Md)  ------ Petitioner
 Vs.
Artha Rin Adalat & others  ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana J : This rule Nisi was issued calling in question the orders dated 25-04- 2007 and 23-07-2008 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Chapai Nababgonj in Artha Decree Execution Case No.03 of 2007 issuing warrant of arrest against this petitioner under section 34 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. 

 3. The respondent No. 2, Manager, United Commercial Bank Limited, Chapai Nababgonj filed Artha Rin Suit No.2 of 2006 against this petitioner and others for realization of outstanding loan. That suit was decreed exported by the judgment and order dated 25-4-2007. Thereafter, on 14-3-2007 the decree-holder bank filed Artha Decree Execution Case No.3 of 2007 on the basis of that decree. On the very date of filing of that execution case the decree-holder bank filed an application praying for issuance of warrant of arrest against the judgment debtors and the learned Judge fixed 19-3-2007 for hearing of that application. Ultimately on 25-4-2007 the learned Judge of the Adalat allowed that application and issued warrant of arrest against this writ- petitioner by one of the impugned orders. Subsequently, by the other impugned order dated 23-7-2008 the learned Judge of the Adalat again issued warrant of arrest against the judgment debtors. The writ-petitioner thereafter has filed this present writ-petition challenging these impugned orders on the main ground that no notice under section 30 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 was issued at all in that execution case before passing of the impugned order issuing warrant of arrest against the judgment-debtors. 

 6. The learned Advocate for the writ-petitioner has made submission mainly to the effect that the writ-petitioner was not made aware of the filing of this execution case by serving any notice as per section 30 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, that the provision of section 30 of the Artha Rin AdalatAin, 2003 is mandatory and that after filing of the execution case and registration thereof the first action required to be taken was to make the judgment- debtor aware of filing of that execution case by serving notice of that case upon them. The learned Advocate has argued that since no such notice under section 30 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 was issued at all in this execution case all the orders passed in this execution case are illegal. The learned Advocate for the writ-petitioner has argued also that the impugned orders issuing warrant of arrest have been illegal for the reason also that before passing of these orders no order for civil imprisonment of the judgment-debtors as per section 34 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 was passed. The learned Advocate has submitted that section 34 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 has provided for civil imprisonment of the judgment-debtors for a maximum period of 6(six) months for the purpose of making the judgment-debtors compelled to pay the decreetal amount and that this section 34 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 does not say anything as to issuance of warrant of arrest against the judgment-debtors. The learned Advocate has contended that since in this case no order for civil imprisonment of the judgment-debtors was passed the impugned orders issuing warrant of arrest against them have been illegal. 

 9. From the annexure-'C' the order sheet of the execution case in question it appears that the execution case was filed on 14-3-2007 and on that very date the decree-holder bank filed an application praying for issuance of warrant of arrest against the judgment-debtors. Ultimately on 25-4-2007 the learned Judge of the Adalat allowed that application and issued warrant of arrest against the judgment- debtors including this petitioner. But it appears from this annexure- 'C' that after filing and registration of this execution case no notice under section 30 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 was at all issued. The provision of section 30 of Artha Rin Adalat, 2003 is mandatory which must be complied with in order to make the judgment-debtors informed of the filing of the execution case against them. But in this case, admittedly, no notice under section 30 of the Artha Rin Ain, 2003 was issued at all by the Adalat concerned and the judgment-debtors, therefore, were not notified as to filing of this execution case against them. The execution cases under Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 are filed for the purpose of realization of the decreetal money and the provision of service of notice as per section 30 has been incorporated in this Ain to make the judgment-debtors aware of filing of the execution case and thereby to give them opportunity for payment of the decreetal amount and all the subsequent actions in such execution case are taken for realization of the decreetal amount if the judgment-debtors,  in spite of being notified of filling of the execution case, do not pay decreetal money. In the present case since no notice under section 30 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 was issued at all the subsequent actions for arresting the judgment- debtors in order to make them compelled to pay the decreetal amount have been illegal. 

 10. Section 34 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 has empowered the Adalat to detain the judgment-debtors in civil jail for a maximum period of 6(six) months for the purpose making them compelled to pay the decreetal money and the Adalat, after passing order for such civil imprisonment, can issue warrant of arrest against such judgment- debtors for making them available for serving out that civil imprisonment. So, before issuing warrant of arrest the Adalat is to pass specific order of civil imprisonment for a specific period. But in this case the Adalat did not pass any order imposing on the petitioner. For this reason also the impugned order issuing warrant of arrest against the petitioner has been illegal. 

 12. But we are unable to accept this contention of the learned Advocate in the present case. In this case the petitioner is not an accused of any criminal case. The civil imprisonment which can be imposed on him under section 34(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is only for the purpose of making him compelled to pay the decreetal amount and not for punishing him for committing any criminal offence. 

 This very section 34(1) itself clearly tells that the civil imprisonment which is imposed on the judgment-debtors under this section is not any punishment for committing any offence, rather it is only for the purpose of making them compelled to pay the decreetal money.
